previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with diarrhea and a low-grade fever. He has a history of HCV cirrhosis, portopulmonary hypertension, and recent hospitalization for similar symptoms. Workup revealed no infectious cause for diarrhea, which was attributed to Remodulin therapy. Blood cultures grew Acinetobacter from his tunneled central line, leading to line removal, temporary central access, and a 14-day course of meropenem. A new PICC was successfully placed. He underwent therapeutic paracentesis for refractory ascites, with albumin administration. Diuretics were increased, and home medications adjusted. He improved clinically, completed antibiotic therapy, and was discharged home with plans to restart ciprofloxacin, monitor for infection clearance, and coordinate tunneled line replacement.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Evaluation for PICC placement.

COMPARISON:  Portable chest x-ray from ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, the course of the
right-sided PICC line is unremarkable, the tip of the line projects over the
lower SVC.  There is no evidence of complications, notably no pneumothorax. 
Unchanged course of the nasogastric tube.  Low lung volumes, but no evidence
of acute lung disease.

INDICATION:  Hepatitis C cirrhosis with ascites.  Needs diagnostic and
therapeutic paracentesis.

COMPARISON:  Paracentesis from ___.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___, and Dr. ___.

PREPROCEDURE IMAGING AND FINDINGS:  Limited four-quadrant ultrasound
demonstrates a moderate volume of intraperitoneal ascites.  The largest pocket
was in the left lower quadrant, and targeted for paracentesis.

PROCEDURE:  The procedure, risks, benefits, and alternatives were discussed
with the patient and written informed consent was obtained.  A preprocedure
timeout was performed, discussing the planned procedure, confirming the
patient's identity with three identifiers, and reviewing a checklist per ___
protocol.

Under ultrasound guidance, an entrance site was selected in the left lower
quadrant and the skin was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  8
cc of 1% lidocaine was instilled for local anesthesia.

A 5 ___ ___ catheter was advanced into the peritoneal cavity in the left
lower quadrant.  20 cc of fluid were aspirated for laboratory analysis.  The
tubing was then attached to wall suction and 1.25 L of orange-colored ascites
were aspirated.  A single 0 silk suture was placed in the skin.  The
previously placed suture was removed.  The entrance site was dressed with a
sterile bandage.

The patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate complications. 
Estimated blood loss was minimal.

Dr. ___ attending radiologist, was present and supervising for the
critical portions of the procedure.

IMPRESSION:  Technically successful ultrasound-guided diagnostic and
therapeutic paracentesis with removal of 1.25 L of orange-colored ascites.

INDICATION: ___ year old man with HCV cirrhosis complicated by portopulmonary
syndrome on continuous remodulin. Needs new tunneled line placement.

COMPARISON: Prior chest radiograph from ___.

CLINICIANS: Dr. ___ resident), Dr. ___ fellow) and
Dr. ___ attending) performed the procedure.  Dr ___ was present
and supervising throughout the whole procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
100 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed throughout total intraservice time of
56 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independently trained radiology nurse. Local anesthesia was
provided by 1% lidocaine to the dermis and 1% lidocaine with epinephrine into
the subcutaneous tissues.

FLUORO TIME: 7.6 minutes, 38 mGy.

PROCEDURE:  

Written informed consent was obtained from the patient.  This was performed
after explaining the risks, benefits, alternatives and indications of the
procedure. The patient was transported to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the imaging table.  The right neck was prepped and draped in usual
sterile fashion. A preprocedure huddle and timeout was performed per ___
protocol.

After anesthetizing the skin and subcutaneous tissues, using ultrasound
guidance, the patent and compressible right internal jugular vein was accessed
using standard micropuncture technique. Pre- and post venous access digital
ultrasound images were stored on PACS.  A 0.018 nitinol wire was advanced into
the superior vena cava. After additional anesthesia, a small ___ was made in
the skin.  Micropuncture needle was exchanged with micropuncture sheath.  The
inner cannula and nitinol wire were removed. A ___ wire was advanced into
the right atrium.  Appropriate measurements were made for skin incision four
fingerbreadths below the venotomy site.  The wire was then advanced into the
IVC.

Attention was now turned to creation of a subcutaneous tunnel.  After
additional local anesthesia, a 1-cm skin incision was made.  A 10 ___
tunneled catheter was passed from the incision to the venotomy site with the
aid of a metal tunneling device.  The venotomy tract was dilated with 8 and 10
___ dilators.  Peel-away sheath was passed over the wire.  The wire and
inner cannula were removed and the catheter was passed through the peel-away
sheath.  The peel-away sheath was removed while the catheter was pushed into
the right atrium.  This was confirmed with fluoroscopy demonstrating the
catheter tip in the right atrium.  The lumen withdrew blood and flushed
easily.  Catheter was secured with ___ silk sutures and an additional
pursestring suture was placed. Venotomy site was closed with 2 Vicryl
subcuticular stitch.  Dry sterile dressings were applied.  No immediate
post-procedure complications were noted. The patient tolerated the procedure
well.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of tunneled access catheter through the
right internal jugular vein approach.  The tip is located in the right atrium
and the catheter is ready for use.
